text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior; to begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly how long these symptoms have been occurring and whether they started suddenly or developed gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Not yet ready; I need to determine if the subacute progression of cognitive decline and right leg weakness is due to a specific neurodegenerative process (like early-stage Huntington's disease or a paraneoplastic syndrome) or a structural lesion, so I will request MRI results of the brain and spine to assess for atrophy or mass effects.
